text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:
- Swiss development aid director Walter Fust urged immediate food aid for North Korea and called on the international community to drop political conditions for starting an aid campaign.
- Credit Suisse Group reported a 70 percent boost in net profit to 1,410 million Swiss francs in the first semester.

- Chief executive Lukas Muehlemann of Credit Suisse, which is taking over insurer Winterthur, said in an interview that a hestitant reaction on the Swiss stock market to the merger plan was probably due to overall market weakness rather than unhappiness at the merger.

- The Lucarno film festival, the most important cultural event in Switzerland's Italian-speaking canton Ticino, is also critical for the region's tourist industry because it draws droves of Swiss from other parts of the coutry as well as many foreign tourists.

- Sargans, a small town in the eastern canton of St Gall, wanted to bar a concert by German teenage star Bluemchen by applying a unique local ban on techno music. But local authorities quickly withdrew the ban under a storm of media attention. Reporters and television crews were drawn in when concert organisers released the town council's letter citing the techno ban.

- In Winterthur, a recession-prone industrial town and headquarters of Swiss insurer Winterthur, the insurer's announcement that it would merge with bank group Credit Suisse was received as good news.
